title: Dynamic Ffi Call Cache
objective: Resolve invariant declared-FFI backend, export, parameter-plan, constraint, and result-domain metadata once per generated declaration call site while retaining all per-call value, ownership, range, transaction, and exception validation

oracles: existing dynamic FFI semantics with SAGEJS_NATIVE_DISABLE=1

handoff.summary: Caches invariant dynamic declared-FFI backend/export, specialized parameter validation, constraint indices, result domain, and exception class once per cryptographically identified declaration call site; all value, ownership, range, transactional, result, and exception checks remain per call. Backend replacement is honored when the trusted runtime require function changes. The repeated FmpqMatrix scalar-entry benchmark improved from a 5.23 microsecond uncached median to 4.39 microseconds cached on this host.
risks: A backend that mutates an export in place without replacing the trusted runtime require function keeps the already resolved callable; generated production backends are immutable by contract, while explicit runtime-host replacement remains supported.

The full integration suite had four unrelated or pre-existing failures: one base serialization-count assertion, one stale FFLAS manifest count assertion, and two transient performance/environment failures that passed focused reruns.
next_steps: Integration should cherry-pick this commit and retain the narrow core-runtime byte-budget ratchet.
If dynamic scalar crossings remain important after higher-level bulk APIs, consider generated closure-local constant wire arrays as a separate measured optimization.
